key_insight: Separating fast acoustic oscillations from slow mean motion enables fully resolved, long-time particle simulations while retaining two-way fluid–structure coupling.
engineering_relevance: The framework could support acoustofluidic device design by resolving particle translation, rotation, and surrounding streaming without time-stepping every acoustic cycle.
method: Split dynamics into time-harmonic first-order acoustics and time-averaged second-order flow.
Represent rigid particles using immersed-boundary/Brinkman volume penalization.
Derive order-consistent particle velocities and motion equations, including Stokes-drift contributions.
evidence_signal: Two-dimensional circular-particle simulations show substantial streaming differences between fixed and freely moving particles and complex density effects; elliptical-particle simulations demonstrate coupled translation and rotation.
watch_item: Accurate moving-interface treatment is central, and the abstract does not establish quantitative accuracy or speedup beyond the reported demonstrations.
paper_title: Fully resolved particle dynamics over long time scales in acoustofluidic flows: Theory and numerical simulations
